items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Anaheim Ducks forward Troy Terry is expected to make his 2026-27 season debut on Wednesday as the Ducks play host to the Nashville Predators . Terry, 29, has missed the Ducks’ first 18 games of the 2026-27 regular season while recovering from summer hip surgery. Ducks head coach Joel Quenneville said Tuesday that Terry is “likely” to play as the Ducks welcome the Predators to the Honda Center on Wednesday. In 61 games with the Ducks during the 2025-26 regular season, Terry collected 19 goals and 57 points. The Denver product added three goals and 11 points in 12 playoff contests as the Ducks defeated the Edmonton Oilers in the first round before being eliminated by the Vegas Golden Knights . A four-time 20-goal scorer, Terry has consistently been one of the Ducks’ most dangerous offensive players since establishing himself as an NHL regular in the 2020-21 season. In his absence, the Ducks have gotten off to a 10-7-1 start to the 2026-27 season, posting a plus-3 goal differential. The Ducks originally selected Terry in the fifth round (No. 148 overall) of the 2015 NHL Draft. The 6’0″ right wing spent his first three post-draft seasons playing close to home at the University of Denver, suiting up for Team USA along the way at both the 2017 World Juniors and the 2018 Winter Olympics. Terry signed with the Ducks in 2018 and gradually developed into a top-six scoring forward for the club, topping out with 37 goals and 67 points in 75 games during the 2021-22 season. He played an instrumental role in the Ducks ending their seven-year playoff drought in the 2025-26 season. items.summary: The Montreal Canadiens welcomed Carey Price back to the Bell Centre with a memorable, spine-tingling ovation Tuesday night.
items.body: MONTREAL — The Montreal Canadiens welcomed Carey Price back to the Bell Centre with a memorable, spine-tingling ovation Tuesday night. Canadiens fans cheered for close to four minutes during an on-ice ceremony, wildly serenading their longtime star goaltender with a blend of “Ca-rey! Ca-rey!” and “Olé, Olé” chants ahead of puck drop against the Minnesota Wild. Price, meanwhile, stood beside the team benches, next to the five individual trophies he won over his illustrious career, as he attempted to get a word in. “From the bottom of my heart, the most sincere ‘Merci beaucoup,’” Price told the crowd, his voice trembling. Following team tradition, the Canadiens added Price to their ring of honour after his induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday in Toronto. Price, 39, became the 62nd member of the Canadiens organization to enter the Hall of Fame, capping a remarkable journey that began in the remote community of Anahim Lake, B.C. Growing up, Price’s father, Jerry, flew his son in a four-seat plane 320 kilometres from their hometown to Williams Lake, B.C., three times a week so he could play minor hockey. Price went on to spend his entire 15-year NHL career in Montreal after the Canadiens selected him fifth overall in the 2005 draft, becoming the franchise’s all-time leader with 361 wins. He finished with a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 goals-against average and 49 shutouts in 712 regular-season games. "It's special,” Price, a member of the Ulkatcho First Nation in B.C., said before the game. “I was able to be a part of many ceremonies here, and obviously the rich culture of this franchise speaks for itself. The decision was heavily criticized across the hockey world, including by Jets head coach Scott Arniel. "He gave up on us. It would be nice to finally be done with this," Arniel said. items.body: TORONTO — Count Toronto Maple Leafs GM John Chayka among those not surprised to hear defenceman Chris Tanev 's reaction to the team’s load management plan that will ration his use over the course of the season. Chayka expected as much when asked about Tanev's response at the NHL's general manager meetings on Tuesday in downtown Toronto. “I think it’s natural and actually a good sign that he wants to play every game,” Chayka said. “It’s Chris Tanev. He’s made a career out of being that player and takes a lot of pride in being available to play every night. “From our side, we do have an obligation to the players and to the organization to do the right thing and consider a player’s long-term health. And to do the right thing for the organization for the short-term and long-term. We respect that Chris wants to play.” Tanev, 36, missed all but 11 games last season after sustaining a serious concussion. This season, he suffered an injury on Oct. 10 against the Colorado Avalanche and then missed nine games. Coach Jim Hiller said that while he wished he could have Tanev in the lineup each night, “there’s a plan in place to protect the player and the team.” Chayka said: “We’re taking in a lot of information and making decisions. It’s my decision and I think it’s the right one for the organization.” It’s also not final. If Tanev’s health improves, the Maple Leafs are open to amending their plan. “This is an ongoing discussion,” Chayka said. “As Chris builds up some resiliency and the doctors get comfortable with where he’s at, then we’ll change our minds as it makes sense to do so.” In the here and now, Tanev's situation is just one of a handful that Chayka is monitoring as injuries mount for the Maple Leafs. items.title: Hellebuyck sends mixed message to Jets fans seeking closure
items.summary: In Connor Hellebuyck’s careful attempt to prevent this from becoming a sticky situation, he has completely muddied the waters regarding why he abandoned the only NHL home he has ever known.
items.body: WINNIPEG — In his much-anticipated return to Winnipeg on Tuesday, Connor Hellebuyck desperately tried to keep his story straight. But in his careful attempt to prevent his departure from Winnipeg from becoming a sticky situation, the former franchise goaltender has completely muddied the waters regarding why he abandoned the only NHL home he has ever known. Sitting in front of dozens of reporters at Canada Life Centre, Hellebuyck looked and acted like a man wanting to have his cake and eat it, too. Rather than speak clearly and concisely about the treatment he received from disappointed Canadians and a clear desire to move his family south of the border, Hellebuyck opted to dance around the subject. Only adding insult to injury, Hellebuyck won't even face the music Tuesday against his former team. Despite his insistence that he felt a "duty" to play, New Jersey Devils general manager Sunny Mehta stepped in with a dizzying analytics-led excuse. Citing a "reduction in our expected win probability," Mehta is sitting his all-star goalie. The irony of Hellebuyck demanding out of Winnipeg, where he had full control of his playing time, to join an organization that now dictates his ice time through analytics is too difficult to ignore. But to understand just how brazen it was for Hellebuyck to sit at a table inside Canada Life Centre and ask fans to separate his exit from his legacy, you have to look at how that exit played out. "The day I said I was a Jet for life, I meant it," Hellebuyck said. "But I also didn't foresee the future that was going to happen." That future turned out to be a sudden and steep decline for a team that had claimed the Presidents' Trophy as the NHL's best regular-season team just a year earlier. items.title: NHL to explore replay assist technology for officials
items.summary: NHL commissioner Gary Bettman was quick to remind that wholesale changes won’t be coming to the way the game is officiated, but he mentioned how tech advancements might streamline everything from information to the flow of the game.
items.body: TORONTO — Remember a few weeks ago when Buffalo’s Owen Power was incensed that he was wrongly whistled for a high-sticking penalty? It was friendly fire. Power didn’t high-stick Matvei Michkov, who was done dirty by his own teammate, Trevor Zegras. All 18,000 fans in KeyBank Arena in Buffalo saw it on replay. The NHL’s Situation Room saw it in near real time. But once the call is made on the ice, according to current rules, there’s no chance to review it and it cannot be rescinded. “The only four people that don’t get to see it are the four guys in striped shirts,” NHL senior executive vice president of hockey operations Colin Campbell said. “There’s times we would like to get involved.” To that end, Campbell said the NHL will explore in the coming months how things like rapid replay assist technology can aid on-ice officials. Think something that wouldn’t involve a long huddle or review, but how quickly, as in the NFL, the spot of the ball is corrected, or how fast it is relayed to the officiating team that a runner stepped out of bounds. “The game’s not perfect,” Campbell said. “How can we help them out? “You look at football, what they’ve done with the quarterback’s helmet. You look at baseball, with the pitcher and catcher (pitchcom device). All sports are expanding communication.” The discussion was brought to the NHL’s 32 general managers in their meeting on Tuesday and Campbell said the “appetite was good.” Rule changes cannot be enacted mid-season but can be voted on in Florida in March for the Competition Committee to implement for 2027-28. items.summary: Michkov, the No. 7 overall pick in 2023, has 14 points in 20 games to start his third NHL season.
items.body: According to a report from NHL insider Kevin Weekes of ESPN, Michkov would prefer to have a fresh start with another team, with Weekes referring to him as a “very, very much in-demand potential trade target.” Michkov is in his third NHL season after the Flyers selected him with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2023 NHL Draft. Michkov made the jump to North America after spending the 2023-24 season with HK Sochi of the KHL, and as a rookie, he notched 63 points on 26 goals and 37 assists in 80 games played, a year good enough for him to finish in fourth place in the voting for the Calder Trophy as the NHL’s top rookie. Last year, Michkov saw his ice time decline from 16:41 as a rookie to 14:50 under head coach Rick Tocchet, who publicly criticized Michkov for showing up to training camp out of shape, raising significant questions about the relationship between Philadelphia’s new head coach and one of its foundational young players. Michkov finished the 2025-26 campaign with 51 points in 81 games. The Flyers performed well last season en route to an appearance in the second round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs, but the team has struggled mightily out of the gate this year. Philadelphia owns a 5-10-5 record, the worst in the Eastern Conference by points percentage. Michkov has earned more ice time from Tocchet this season, up to 15:54 per game, and he leads the Flyers with 10 goals. Combined with his four assists, his point total sits at 14, good for a tie for the team lead alongside Trevor Zegras. Michkov is set to be a restricted free agent upon the conclusion of this season. According to ESPN’s Emily Kaplan , the Flyers have not been made aware of a direct trade request from Michkov’s camp.

items.title: NHL, NHLPA to discuss possibility of ‘smoothing’ salary cap over next two seasons
items.summary: The NHL’s salary cap will be $113.5 million next season, and is projected to be $127.5 million in the 2028-29 season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The NHL’s salary cap has increased substantially over the last couple of seasons, leading to some monstrous contracts getting handed out this past offseason. It’s expected to continue to skyrocket in the years to come. According to Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman , however, the league is looking at the possibility of “smoothing” the salary cap’s growth over the next two seasons. At Tuesday’s GM meetings, it was decided that the NHL and NHLPA will meet in the new year to discuss ways of making the salary cap’s increases over the next couple seasons less dramatic year over year, with the hopes of creating a more stable salary environment across the league. The NHL’s salary cap this season is $104 million, which increased from $95.5 million last season and $88 million the season prior. It will grow to $113.5 million next season, and is currently projected to be $127.5 million in the 2028-29 season. According to Friedman, one strategy the league could pursue is raising next season’s cap from $113.5 million by a certain amount, and then lowering the 2028-29 cap by the same amount, thereby shrinking the cap spike between the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons. For example, if next year’s cap is raised from $113.5 to $115.5 million, representing a $2 million bump, then the cap for the 2028-29 season would be decreased by $2 million, going from a projected $127.5 million to a projected $125.5 million. This would keep the difference between the 2027-28 and 2028-29 salary caps to $10 million. items.title: Canucks quarter-mark report: Few bright spots in dark days of rebuild
items.summary: There has been no joy for the Canucks so far. And on several nights, some essential pride has been missing too, as Vancouver crashed to its worst opening quarter in franchise history.
items.body: VANCOUVER — Losing hockey games is not the same thing as playing losing hockey. Coach Manny Malhotra warned everyone about this ahead of the first full season of the Vancouver Canucks ’ rebuild. “There’s a very big difference between losing games, which is inevitable. . . and playing losing hockey,” Malhotra told reporters on the eve of training camp in September. “The measure of our group will be on playing the right way, doing the things that we’re talking about, having details to your game, which is going to give us an opportunity to win. That’s where the pride or the joy will come from: knowing that we are learning, we’re doing the things that we’re asked, and it’s getting better.” There has been no joy for the Canucks so far. What’s worse, on several nights, some of that essential pride has been missing, too, as Vancouver crashed to its worst opening quarter in franchise history. items.summary: Minnesota has also assigned forward Tyler Pitlick to the AHL’s Iowa Wild.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images The Minnesota Wild are welcoming their captain back into the fold. On Tuesday, the Wild announced that they have activated defenseman Jared Spurgeon off of injured reserve. In a corresponding move, the Wild have assigned forward Tyler Pitlick to their American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Iowa Wild. Spurgeon, 36, has missed Minnesota’s last five games , and was also out for a four-game stretch with an upper-body injury earlier this season. In 10 games played so far, the Edmonton native has a goal and four assists for five points while averaging about 20 and a half minutes of ice time. Last season, Spurgeon notched six goals and 16 assists for 22 points in 79 games while averaging about 19 and a half minutes of ice time. He then put up no goals and an assist while averaging a tick over 21 minutes in 11 playoff games. Selected by the New York Islanders in the sixth round of the 2008 NHL Entry Draft, Spurgeon did not sign his entry-level deal with New York and instead signed with Minnesota after his five-year junior career with the Spokane Chiefs of the Western Hockey League (WHL). Spurgeon is now in his 17th NHL season, all with the Wild. He ranks second in games played on Minnesota’s all-time list with 1,022, just six games back of Mikko Koivu. He also ranks third on the Wild’s all-time scoring list with 443 points. He is in the final season of a seven-year, $53.03 million contract . Pitlick, 35, has gone scoreless in 12 games played for Minnesota this season. The Minneapolis, Minnesota native has played for nine different teams over parts of 12 seasons in the NHL. Minnesota kicks off a three-game road trip against the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday before visiting the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday.

items.title: NHL, NHLPA to discuss salary-cap options in new year
items.body: Frank Seravalli will have a full recap of today’s GM meetings later today on sportsnet.ca, but a quickie blog on one additional item from Tuesday's meetup. The NHL and NHLPA will meet in the new year to discuss the possibility of “smoothing” the salary cap over the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons. Under the current three-year agreement — which concludes at the end of next season — the salary cap for 2027-28 will be $113.5 million. At September’s Board of Governors meeting in New York City, the league provided a preliminary estimate of $127.5 million for 2028-29. What the league and players’ association could agree to is raising next season’s ceiling and lowering the 2028-29 number by the same amount. For example, if they decided to raise 2027-28 by $2 million to $115.5 million, they would drop the following year to $125.5 million. Again, there is nothing concrete at this time, just a willingness to discuss the issue over the next few months. The NBA went through something similar after a major television contract jumped its cap from $70 million in 2015-16 to $94 million in 2016-17. After it was decided that summer created too much carnage, the latest CBA prevents any jump being larger than 10 per cent. We’ll see what the NHL and NHLPA come up with, if both agree on a change.

items.body: Connor Hellebuyck is giving a bit of insight in his decision to request a trade from the Winnipeg Jets . Returning to Winnipeg for the first time since being traded on Oct. 23, the New Jersey Devils goaltender said incidents with his family played a significant role in his decision. "There's no one singular moment that wasn't important in all of this decision making, and this is over a span of time," Hellebuyck told reporters in Winnipeg on Tuesday. "I will say, with all the uncertainty, there was, you know, some moments and some things that happened to my family that, for me, crossed the line. As a husband and a father, I felt (the incidents) made that decision very certain." Though Hellebuyck didn't specify what happened to his family, he said "it was more than online death threats." Hellebuyck was dealt from the Jets to conclude a long saga that saw the goalie suspended by his team after failing to report for training camp. The 33-year-old has three Vezina Trophies and a Hart Trophy as league MVP under his belt, all won as a member of the Jets. He backstopped the United States to Olympic gold — their first in four decades — at the 2026 Winter Olympics. items.title: Report: NHL GMs ‘warm’ to idea of video-assisted review for officials
items.summary: Plays in question would help refs get the call right on penalties they might’ve missed or mistakenly called.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Christopher Trim-Imagn Images If there hasn’t been enough video review in the game today, just wait. According to insider Frank Seravalli, NHL executive vice president and director of hockey operations Colin Campbell stated that, during a meeting among the league’s general managers on Tuesday, a discussion of video-assisted review took place. The idea is that there will be direct communication to on-ice officials to amend penalties, most notably friendly-fire high-sticking. Per Seravalli, Campbell said reception from the GMs was “warm.” There is a potential vote coming up in March, with any rule changes being implemented for the 2027-28 season. Any potential rule change would also have to be approved by the NHL Players’ Association. According to responses on social media, fans seem to be in favor of the idea of righting any wrongs by referees. The one concern would be what the video review process would be like and, more or less, how long it would take. These days, if there is a call that officials feel like they messed up on, the second ref would come over to discuss the play before making a decision to reverse the call. If there were VAR put in place for penalties, many around the game hope that it can be a quick fix, rather than a long, drawn-out review that we sometimes see for potential offsides or goalie interference penalties. There certainly would be positives in helping out the refs, who can sometimes miss infractions in real time, especially with how fast the game is played these days.

items.summary: Jake Middleton wears his family history on his left arm, quite literally. The Flames defenceman’s grandfather served in the Second World War, and Middleton shares his love with a deeply meaningful tattoo sleeve.
items.body: CALGARY — The poppy fell from his father's chest and into the grave. Jake Middleton was seven years old, standing among family and friends near the military base in Wainwright, Alta., watching as they lowered his grandfather, Robert Bruce, into the ground. Somewhere in the emotion of that moment, it came loose and tumbled onto the coffin below. One by one, those gathered for “Papa's” funeral removed their own poppies, stepped forward and tossed them into the grave, sending their final tribute down with the man they had come to say goodbye to. And every Nov. 11, when the trumpets begin to sound, that little boy comes rushing back. "You know, I always get a frog in my throat when those start playing on Remembrance Day," said the Calgary Flames defenceman. It's a memory that has never really left him. Neither has the man who inspired it. Middleton wears his family history on his left arm, quite literally. His extensive tattoo sleeve is a deeply personal tribute to his grandfather, a Second World War dispatch rider who served in North Africa, France, Germany and England. It's a remarkable piece of work, and Middleton has never been particularly shy about showing it off. Those familiar with his entertaining media availabilities know they’re often delivered shirtless. items.body: A player with a very impressive junior-hockey resume is on the verge of getting his first NHL shot. Sam O'Reilly has been recalled by the Tampa Bay Lightning , the club announced Tuesday. O'Reilly was MVP of the OHL regular season and playoffs as well as the Memorial Cup last season after leading the Kitchener Rangers to the CHL and OHL titles. He was acquired by the Rangers in a mid-season deal with the London Knights, with whom he also won a Memorial Cup and two OHL championships. O'Reilly, 20, also had eight points in seven games for bronze medal-winning Canada at last year's world junior championship. The Toronto native has two goals and four assists in 12 games with AHL Syracuse. The Lightning acquired O'Reilly in a deal with the Edmonton Oilers for Isaac Howard in July 2025. items.title: Wild could keep unsigned Quinn Hughes past trade deadline, GM says
items.body: The Minnesota Wild are going all-in on their Stanley Cup aspirations this season, even if it means losing their star defenceman to free agency. General manager Bill Guerin said Tuesday that the team might opt to keep Quinn Hughes past the trade deadline even if he does not re-sign with the Wild, running the risk of losing the one-time Norris Trophy winner for nothing. “Honestly, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes, so I mean, I want to keep him as long as I possibly can,” Guerin told reporters in Toronto, per NHL.com . “Whether it’s three months, three years, seven years, whatever, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes.” When asked if that would extend to keeping an unsigned Hughes past the trade deadline, Guerin said yes. Hughes, in the final year of a six-year, $47.1-million contract, became eligible to re-sign with the Wild on July 1. On that front, Guerin said progress towards a deal remains "status quo." "Honestly, I just want him to focus on hockey,” Guerin said. “Like I said, he knows what’s going on in his head. He understands everything.” The Wild acquired Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks in December 2025 in exchange for Zeev Buium, Liam Ohgren, Marco Rossi and a 2026 first-round pick.

Most of the attention Tuesday night will be on former Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, who demanded a trade out of Winnipeg in the offseason and forced a move him to New Jersey a few weeks ago. items.body: TORONTO -- All is quiet between the Minnesota Wild and Quinn Hughes , and the team could keep the defenseman past the NHL Trade Deadline on March 1 if he doesn’t sign a new deal, general manager Bill Guerin said Tuesday. Hughes, whom the Wild acquired from the Vancouver Canucks in a trade Dec. 12, 2025, is in the final season of a six-year, $47.1 million contract ($7.85 million average annual value) he signed with Vancouver on Oct. 3, 2021. The 27-year-old has been eligible to sign a new contract with the Wild since July 1. If he doesn’t sign before June 30, he will become an unrestricted free agent the next day. On Oct. 24, Hughes said he “wouldn’t be surprised if something happens soon.” But Tuesday, Guerin said the situation is “status quo.” “Because, honestly, I just want him to focus on hockey,” Guerin said. “Like I said, he knows what’s going on in his head. He understands everything.” Would Guerin be willing to keep Hughes past the trade deadline? Hughes won the Norris Trophy as the NHL’s best defenseman in 2024. Since the trade, Hughes has 79 points (11 goals, 68 assists) in 67 games, second on the Wild and second among NHL defensemen. In that span, forward Kirill Kaprizov leads Minnesota with 86 points (43 goals, 43 assists) in 66 games, and Evan Bouchard of the Edmonton Oilers is first among NHL defensemen with 98 points (26 goals, 72 assists) in 70 games. The Wild (12-3-4) lead the Central Division entering their game at the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday (7 p.m. ET; RDS, TSN5, MINNHL, Wild+). “Honestly, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes, so I mean, I want to keep him as long as I possibly can,” Guerin said. “Whether it’s three months, three years, seven years, whatever, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes.”

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images It’s official: a former NHL sniper is heading overseas. On Tuesday, the Kontinental Hockey League announced that former NHL winger Evander Kane has signed a one-year contract with HC Sibir Novosibirsk. Kane signs with Sibir, even though multiple reports stated that he was receiving offers from teams on this side of the Atlantic. His agent, Dan Milstein, stated that Kane would be heading to the KHL during last week’s episode of DFO Rundown . The 35-year-old moves to Russia after spending the 2025-26 season with the Vancouver Canucks . On a team that finished with the worst record in the NHL, Kane managed to score 13 goals and 18 assists for 31 points, finishing sixth on the team in scoring, while appearing in 71 games. It came after a rather successful four seasons with the Edmonton Oilers , where Kane’s physical play and scoring touch helped his team reach the Western Conference Finals three times, advancing to the Stanley Cup Final in 2024 and 2025. In 1,001 regular-season games, which included stops with the Buffalo Sabres , San Jose Sharks and Winnipeg Jets (formerly the Atlanta Thrashers), Kane potted 339 goals and 309 assists for 648 pints, with another 55 points in 97 postseason contests. This won’t be the first time Kane has played in Russia. During the lockout that canceled half of the 2012-13 season, he signed with Dynamo Minsk, scoring two points in 12 games. Sibir is 8-1-4-13 so far this season, sitting with the worst record in the KHL’s Eastern Conference and 20th in the league’s overall standings. According to the KHL , Evander Kane has signed a one-year contract with Sibir Novosibirsk in the KHL. Earlier in November, in speaking to David Pagnotta on DFO Insider , Dan Milstein of Gold Star Hockey confirmed that Evander Kane would sign with a KHL organization and that a formal announcement should be expected in the next few days; the team has officially come to light. Because of his age and poor play during last season with the Vancouver Canucks, Milstein’s announcement strongly suggests that Kane won’t return to the NHL. Although there were plenty of ups and downs, few players get to enjoy a 16-year career like Kane did. That career began on June 26, 2009, when the Atlanta Thrashers selected Kane with the fourth overall pick in the 2009 NHL Draft. He immediately jumped to the NHL, scoring 14 goals and 26 points in 66 games, good for a ninth-place finish in Calder Trophy voting. Kane spent one more season with the Thrashers and remained with the team when they relocated, becoming the second iteration of the Winnipeg Jets. His first season in Winnipeg is arguably his career-best campaign. The Vancouver, BC, native finished second on the team in scoring behind Blake Wheeler , registering 30 goals and 57 points in 74 games with a +11 rating. A few weeks before the 2012-13 campaign was supposed to start, the Jets signed Kane to a six-year, $31.5MM ($5.25MM AAV) extension. Unfortunately, Kane’s relationship with the Jets rapidly began to sour. Toward the end of the 2013-14 campaign, Kane was accused of assault in his hometown and was subsequently sued for financial damages.

On the other hand, an 84-game season, divided by four, means the Canucks have one more game to avoid manufacturing the NHL’s worst opening quarter since the salary-cap era began in 2005. So, despite an array of gruesome numbers surrounding the Canucks, arithmetic may still be their friend. They could use one. items.title: Stenberg leads Sharks past Islanders in shootout to stop 5-game skid
items.body: SAN JOSE, Calif. — Ivar Stenberg scored the only goal in a shootout that lasted eight rounds, and the San Jose Sharks beat the New York Islanders 3-2 on Monday night to snap a five-game losing streak. Tyler Toffoli had a goal and an assist, and Stenberg also scored in regulation for the Sharks (8-11-1). Stenberg has six goals and is tied for the scoring lead among NHL rookies. Ben Hutton and Victor Eklund scored for the Islanders (7-6-4), who have lost four straight games (0-2-2). Ilya Sorokin stopped 37 shots. Stenberg put the Sharks on the board late in the first period after Toffoli sent a shot toward the net. Stenberg got a piece of the puck to redirect it past Sorokin and tie the game at 1. San Jose again rallied from a goal down midway through the second when Toffoli’s shot deflected off Islanders defenseman Adam Pelech and into the net. It was Toffoli’s first goal in eight games. Hutton opened the scoring early in the first after Simon Holmstrom’s pass found him with an open look. Eklund put New York ahead 2-1 early in the second with a power-play goal. Sharks center Alexander Wennberg, who returned after missing 10 games, was called for the penalty that led to the power play. The game got chippy late in the second as fights broke out, leading to four five-minute major penalties. Barclay Goodrow received a penalty for fighting Mitchell Chaffee, and Ty Dellandrea was penalized for fighting Kyle MacLean.

Ahead of the milestone game, head coach Spencer Carbery remarked on how quickly Leonard has gone from an exciting young prospect to an established NHL player. Before that, though, Leonard made perhaps an even bigger splash — having a fun night out with Alex Ovechkin that went viral . “Well, you can’t forget Boston, Ovi taking him out with the boys on the BC campus, right?” Carbery said. “I saw those videos surfacing from that. It was great to see.” Leonard, fresh out of college hockey, met up with a group of Caps players, including Ovechkin and Jakob Chychrun , for sushi upon Washington’s plane landing, just hours after Leonard signed his first professional contract in Boston College’s locker room . Leonard was initially stunned by Ovechkin’s text message asking to meet up and explore his college campus, and he even paused to wonder with his BC teammates if it was fake before replying. “They were like, ‘What? "Wow, this might be the first time a Tkachuk has ever received a warm welcome in Toronto," Keith Tkachuk said in his opening remark. It was a joke that he went back to at the end of a 10-minute speech in which he mentioned and honored many former teammates, coaches and executives who acquired him and traded him and acquired him again. He brought up his cousin, former NHLer Tom Fitzgerald, who he said "showed me and many others what it took to be a longtime NHL leader and champion." "Winnipeg is also where I would first understand and respect the privilege of playing in the NHL." He especially thanked Joe Yannetti, the Jets' Boston-based scout, for never wavering on him despite the fact that he broke his ankle in his draft year and missed a lot of time. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Philadelphia’s Travis Sanheim preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to the goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 19:38 (0:22 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.title: McDavid’s historic assist streak ends in Oilers’ win over Rangers
items.body: For a second on Monday, it appeared that Connor McDavid had extended his historic assist streak to 19 games right at the buzzer in the Edmonton Oilers ' 3-1 win over the New York Rangers. But after a quick ruling from the NHL, McDavid had his helper on Leon Draisaitl's empty-net goal pulled off the scoresheet. As the Rangers pressed on the power play with their net empty in the final two minutes, a rebound came out to McDavid in front of the Oilers' net. Edmonton's captain bumped into New York forward JT Miller in the battle for the puck, which was eventually tipped out to Draisaitl closer to the blue line, where No. 29 flipped it down the ice and into the open cage. Upon closer inspection, Miller's stick was the last to touch the puck before Draisaitl put the game away — bringing McDavid's streak to an end at 18. With assists in 18 straight games, McDavid tied Adam Oates for the second-longest streak in NHL history, behind only Wayne Gretzky’s 23 games set in 1990-91. He did continue his point streak to open the season, however, opening the scoring with his 11th goal in Edmonton's first 19 games — giving him 48 points on the year.

items.summary: If there is one thread that ties the Hockey Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, it might be the sheer improbability of their paths to the hallowed Hall.
items.body: TORONTO — If there is one thread that ties the Hockey Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, it might be the sheer improbability of their paths to the hallowed Hall. Of course, breathing the rarefied air fewer than four percent of the game’s all-time roster has shared is reserved for only a select few, but this class faced some of the longest odds before their inductions on Monday night in downtown Toronto. Generational goaltender Carey Price hailed from Ulkatcho First Nation in Anahim Lake, B.C. “Growing up in a remote community, there was a very slim chance of this happening without a relentless desire and opportunity,” Price said in his induction speech on Monday. For Cindy Curley, her path to playing competitive hockey ended at Providence College — until the creation of the women’s world championship. “I’m often called a pioneer,” Curley said. “But I’d like to think I just grew up with hockey.” Builder inductee Brian Burke didn’t play hockey until he moved to Minnesota as a teenager and got hooked on the State of Hockey’s historic high school tournament. “Nobody starts playing hockey at 13 in Minnesota and says I’m going to be in the Hockey Hall of Fame, unless you’re an idiot,” Burke said. “Not a god damn chance you think about it. Life is funny.” Patrice Bergeron burst onto the scene as an 18-year-old rookie but the player the Boston Bruins chose over Joe Thornton to build around also faced a career crossroads in his 20s when he missed nearly an entire season with multiple concussions. "It was a no-brainer for us," Saros, the Nashville Predators goalie, told NHL.com on the red carpet that led to the Hockey Hall of Fame induction ceremony. "A once-in-a-lifetime situation, so we wanted to show up for this." The Predators play in Los Angeles on Tuesday, but Forsberg, Josi and Saros, three of Rinne's longest-tenured teammates and some of his closest friends in the game, were part of the Nashville contingent that was here to honor Rinne and his induction as part of the Class of 2026. They arrived Monday, got to the Hall of Fame in time for the ceremony, and Forsberg said they were planning to leave right when it ended or even before. They'll arrive in Los Angeles after midnight and be in the lineup against the Kings on Tuesday. "We were asked if we wanted to come and it was a very easy answer," Forsberg said. "The logistics were handled very well and we'll be there (Tuesday). They did a great job putting all this together and making it reasonable without losing any focus." Vasquez-US PRESSWIRE Keith Tkachuk celebrated his three children and the rest of his family as the former NHLer gave his Hockey Hall of Fame induction speech in Toronto Monday night. “To my children, Matthew, Brady and Taryn: Being your father is the greatest title I’ve ever had,” Keith Tkachuk said. “Taryn, you are a smart, strong, beautiful, quick witted, and may have the most hockey knowledge in the family. Brady, you’re the most caring and thoughtful person I know. Matthew, you made me a father for the first time and filled me with joy. I didn’t know it was possible.” The father said watching his two sons play with the U.S. Olympic men’s hockey team, and now with the Florida Panthers , “has been the thrill of a lifetime.” Keith Tkachuk was inducted as part of the 2026 Hall of Fame class, along with Carey Price, Patrice Bergeron, Cindy Curley, Pekka Rinne and Brian Burke. “This game has welcomed me at every level. I accept this honour with gratitude to everyone who has been part of my journey,” Keith Tkachuk said. It’s been a busy week for Keith Tkachuk. Last Saturday in Toronto, the 54-year-old retired winger was booed as we was introduced with his fellow inductees before the Toronto Maple Leafs hosted the New Jersey Devils in the annual Hockey Hall of Fame Game. Keith Tkachuk had 538 goals and 527 assists for 1,065 points and 2,219 penalty minutes in 1,201 regular-season games with the Winnipeg Jets , Phoenix Coyotes , St. Louis Blues and Atlanta Thrashers. items.body: Carey Price first visited the Hockey Hall of Fame as a teenager. The former Montreal Canadiens goaltender joked over the weekend he wouldn't mind trying one of the interactive games — specifically featuring a netminder sporting very familiar equipment — that sits among the many tributes to the sport's rich history. "It's pretty special to be able to look around," Price said before adding with a smile: "I was hoping to get the chance to shoot on myself downstairs." The 39-year-old was once at the pinnacle of his craft. Now he's taken his place alongside the game's greats. Price was inducted into the Hall as part of the 2026 class alongside Patrice Bergeron, Pekka Rinne, Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley in the player category Monday. Brian Burke was enshrined as a builder. "When I was a kid, I had a dream that I can vividly remember," Price, who sported the Canadiens' red, white and blue for all 15 of his NHL seasons, said during his speech in downtown Toronto. "I was walking down a red carpet, just like in the Bell Centre. As I was walking, I approached a mountain of a figure. The No. 5 pick at the 2005 draft, Price won the Hart Trophy as league MVP and the Vezina Trophy as its top goaltender in 2015. The Anahim Lake, B.C., product finished with a 361-261-79 record, .917 save percentage, 2.51 goals-against average and 49 shutouts across 712 regular-season games in a career cut short by injury. Price had even better numbers in high-pressure moments before a knee issue ended his playing days beyond the 2021-22 campaign. He owned a .919 save percentage, 2.39 GAA and eight shutouts in 92 playoff contests, with his final post-season at the top of the list — willing the underdog Canadiens on an improbable push to the 2021 Stanley Cup final. items.body: Register Login Mammoth Recall Zac Jones By Brian La Rose | at November 9, 2026 9:00 pm After returning Gregor Biber to AHL Tucson before he had a chance to play a game, it seemed likely that the Mammoth would be bringing someone else up to serve as a reserve option. They’ve now done just that, announcing ( Twitter link ) that they’ve recalled blueliner Zac Jones from Tucson. The 26-year-old is in his first season with Utah after inking a two-year, two-way contract following a non-tender by Buffalo back in June. Jones cleared waivers in training camp and has been with the Roadrunners since then. He’s off to a hot start as well, notching 11 points in 13 games to start the year. While Jones hasn’t seen any NHL action this season, he has a fair bit of experience at the top level. He has 115 games under his belt, all coming over parts of five seasons with the Rangers, who drafted him in the third round back in 2019. Jones has four goals and 24 assists in those outings in a little under 16 minutes per night of playing time. Even with Nate Schmidt out day-to-day, there’s no guarantee that Jones will see any ice time while on recall. He could just wind up being the seventh defender which would enable Artem Duda to remain in the lineup. Alternatively, if they want a bit more offensive upside on the back end, they could try Jones on the third pairing in the coming days.

In a recent appearance on 102.5 The Game ( audio link ), Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman suggested that the change won’t be off the ice, which suggests that head coach Jeff Blashill’s job isn’t in jeopardy. Instead, Chicago’s preference would be to make a move to shake up the roster. For the young firepower that Chicago has, they sit dead last in goals per game so far this season. Rookie Roman Kantserov has lived up to the hype with eight contests in 17 games as well. However, things thin out after that. Patrick Kane has eight assists but only one goal. Pittsburgh is 6-10-2 to start the year and sits at the bottom of the Eastern Conference, with little indication they will climb out of their poor start. The Penguins aren’t a quick team; they don’t play well defensively and lack toughness. They are also quite old by NHL standards, which is likely why they appear ready to start moving some of the older Penguins. Pittsburgh has several pending veteran UFAs, but two players remain useful and have another year on their deals. Those two players are Rickard Rakell and Bryan Rust , two veteran wingers who have been available via trade for over a year now and likely had suitors in the past. Now, with Pittsburgh in the spot it is in and those players another year older, it’s fair to wonder whether Pittsburgh will get the same kind of trade offers for those two men that they would have received in years past. In fairness to Pittsburgh, they will likely receive lower offers for any player they put on the market right now, simply because the entire team is struggling. Selling low generally brings out lower trade offers, as the NHL has always been a “What have you done for me lately” league. items.body: Register Login Capitals Recall Justin Holl By Brennan McClain | at November 9, 2026 5:00 pm The Washington Capitals had a roster spot to fill after losing netminder Rémi Poirier off waivers earlier this afternoon. Washington quickly filled it, announcing they recalled defenseman Justin Holl from the AHL’s Hershey Bears. Holl, 34, earns his second call-up of the 2026-27 season. The Capitals signed Holl to a one-year, $900K contract this past offseason and recalled him earlier this season after Washington’s defensive corps suffered a few injuries. He looked good in his debut with Washington, scoring two goals in three games with a +1 rating, while averaging 12:59 of ice time per game. It’s a solid change of pace for Holl after the 10-year blueliner suffered through the worst stretch of his professional career with the Detroit Red Wings. Ahead of the 2023-24 season, the Red Wings signed Holl to a three-year, $10.2MM ($3.4MM AAV) contract after he spent the previous six years with the Toronto Maple Leafs. It started poorly, as Holl finished with only five assists in 38 games in his first season. Holl struggled again during the 2024-25 season, prompting Detroit to demote him. Last campaign, the final season of his three-year pact, Holl played exclusively for the Grand Rapids Griffins in the AHL before he was traded to the St. Louis Blues as a salary offset for the Justin Faulk trade. In fairness to Holl, he was never known as an offensive threat, but his production in Detroit was far lower than he was accustomed to in Toronto. Still, he also began to struggle defensively, producing a career-worst takeaway-to-turnover ratio in the 2024-25 season. Regardless, he has appeared far more comfortable in his limited action with the Capitals.

items.summary: Only two games were on the WWC schedule on Monday, featuring the women’s hockey’s two best teams.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The superpowers of women’s hockey were part of the short, two-game slate on Monday at the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship. Canada and the United States, both favorites to win their respective groups, took on the underdog teams in Denmark and Austria on Tuesday, both trying to prove they belong with the best teams in the world. Let’s look back at what happened in Herning and Esbjerg on Monday, and which players stood out: I mean, both of these games went exactly how we expected them to. Since both games started at the same time, it seemed there was a little race for Austria and Denmark to put their first shot on goal. items.summary: Sheehan was a member of the Montreal Canadiens’ 1971 Stanley Cup championship team.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The hockey world has lost a member of the Montreal Canadiens ‘ 1971 Stanley Cup championship team. On Monday, the NHL Alumni Association announced that former center Bobby Sheehan passed away at the age of 77. The Weymouth, Massachusetts native was selected by the Canadiens out of the Ontario Hockey Association’s St. Catherines Black Hawks in the 1969 NHL Amateur Draft. He spent his first two professional seasons in Montreal’s organization, playing 45 total regular season games with the Canadiens and winning the Stanley Cup with Montreal in 1971. Sheehan joined the California Golden Seals for the 1971-72 season, where he scored 20 goals and added 26 assists for 46 points in 78 games. Following his lone season with the Golden Seals, Sheehan had a three-year stint in the World Hockey Association (WHA). His 1972-73 season with the WHA’s New York Raiders was the best of his career, putting up 35 goals and 53 assists for 88 points in 75 games. He stayed with New York (which would be renamed the New York Golden Blades and then the Jersey Knights) for most of the 1973-74 season before moving on to the Edmonton Oilers through the 1974-75 season. Sheehan returned to the NHL with the Chicago Black Hawks in the 1975-76 season, and then played for the Detroit Red Wings in the 1976-77 season. He went back to the WHA for one last season in 1977-78, when played for the Indianapolis Racers. Sheehan then spent the rest of his career splitting time between the New York Rangers , Colorado Rockies, and Los Angeles Kings of the NHL, the New Haven Nighthawks and Binghamton Whalers of the American Hockey League (AHL), and the Forth Worth Texans of the Central Hockey League (CHL), before retiring in 1983. He had been practicing with the Caps as the club’s third goalie, sitting out of games as a healthy scratch since the club acquired him in a trade from the New Jersey Devils for a 2027 seventh-round draft pick . Some debate remains about whether the Stars can directly assign Poirier to their AHL affiliate, the Texas Stars, if they were the only team to put a claim in on the backstop. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Some unwanted news for a team already experiencing enough struggles this season. When speaking to the media, Columbus Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness announced that forward Conor Garland will not be in the lineup on Tuesday night, when the Blue Jackets take on the Florida Panthers . Bowness said Garland is battling back from an upper-body injury but didn’t provide a timeline for his return. It isn’t quite clear when or where Garland was hurt. He played the entirety of Columbus’ last contest, a 5-2 loss to the Buffalo Sabres this past Friday night. The 30-year-old was a -2 while logging a little over 13 minutes of ice time, not too far from his average for the year. Garland had appeared in each of the Jackets’ first 15 games of the 2026-27 season, but has definitely looked far from the offensive threat he was earlier in his career. He has just one assist to his name to go along with his plus/minus of -5 while averaging 13:33 of ice time per game. This is the Scituate, Mass. native’s first full season in Columbus. He was traded to the Blue Jackets ahead of last year’s trade deadline from the Vancouver Canucks , as he was expected to provide an offensive boost as they battled to stay in the Wild Card race. He scored five goals and seven points in the remaining 21 games, but the Jackets came short of clinching a playoff berth. With Garland out, expect to see Ryan Lomberg back in the lineup, joining Steven Lorentz and Jack Williams on the fourth line during practice on Monday. The Blue Jackets (7-8-0) sit sixth in the Metropolitan Division, six points back of the last Wild Card position in the Eastern Conference.

items.body: A key member of the Toronto Maple Leafs ' future is currently sidelined. Top defence prospect Ben Danford has a broken wrist and is considered week-to-week, Toronto Marlies head coach Steve Sullivan told reporters. The 20-year-old is in his first full AHL season, after joining the Marlies for the 2026 playoffs en route to a Calder Cup. He finished his OHL career last season, after four years split between the Oshawa Generals and Brantford Bulldogs. Danford totalled 99 points in 233 OHL regular-season games and 19 points in 60 playoff contests. The Maple Leafs' No. 31 overall pick in the 2024 NHL Draft had a goal and two assists during the Marlies' playoff run last year, but has taken on a much bigger role this year. items.body: Aho, Kotkaniemi played underground inside Veikkaus Arena during junior hockey careers HELSINKI -- The awe helped beat the jet lag when the Carolina Hurricanes showed up for their first practice at Veikkaus Arena on Monday in preparation for the 2026 NHL Global Series against the Seattle Kraken later this week.​ The Hurricanes trudged into the rink about two hours after landing, the end of an eight-hour overnight flight. Getting a sweat and working the legs are important in beating jet lag, but it's not always fun. This time, though, was different, in part because of the setting. The Hurricanes used the arena's practice rink, known as "The Cave," for a brisk afternoon practice. The rink is two stories underground, carved out of the bedrock upon which the arena is built. The white stone walls and roof contribute to an intimate setting. It's home to the junior team of Jokerit, one of the biggest clubs in Liiga, the top-tier professional league in Finland. Hurricanes forward Sebastian Aho played here when he was a junior player for Karpat's under-20 team. He was raving about it to his teammates on the bus ride from the airport. We are now 41 days into the fantasy season and are witnessing teams start to separate in our league standings. It’s a long season, but we are nearing the quarter-mark. Here’s what we learned in Week 6 of fantasy hockey as we try not to overreact while we question what is happening with our goaltenders right now. Gauthier scored in every game during Week 6, extending his historic goal streak to six games with his 13th goal and 44th shot during that stretch. It is the most goals ever during a six-game span, leaving fantasy owners to wonder if they have a potential 70-goal scorer on their hands. The 22-year-old has really turned it on after a slow start to the 2026-27 campaign, where he potted just two goals in his first 11 games. He is now on pace for a whopping 70 goals and 336 SOG across the full 84-game season after missing one game earlier this year. He also led all skaters with three game-winning goals last week, single-handedly dominating that category. Across the last seven days, a surprising seven teams went undefeated as New Jersey (4), Anaheim (4), Nashville (3), Boston (3), New York Rangers (3), Winnipeg (3) and Ottawa (2) all went without a loss. On the other side of the coin, four teams failed to pick up a win as Chicago (4), San Jose (4), Vancouver (3) and Toronto (3) went without a win in Week 6. With both Michael Misa and Gabriel Perreault joining both their teams’ top power-play unit and top line this past week, we are watching more teams lacking offence turn to their young upcoming superstars for immediate solutions.

TORONTO — Connor Hellebuyck had just recorded his first shutout and fifth straight win of the season when the boos started to rain down at Scotiabank Arena in Toronto on Sunday night. Luckily for him, they were not being directed at the New Jersey Devils goalie — but rather towards the Toronto Maple Leafs , who were jeered by the home crowd after losing for the fifth time in six games. For Hellebuyck, the echoes of boos were supposed to be a small taste of things to come for his highly-anticipated return to Winnipeg on Tuesday. Now he might not even hear them More Videos Following Sunday's win against Toronto, the Devils announced that the 33-year-old would not be starting against the Winnipeg Jets , with GM Sunny Mehta citing a "reduction in our expected win probability" as the primary reason he will sit out. Winnipeg fans, of course, will cite another reason: he's scared to face the fanbase. "I love Winnipeg and playing there again — and just facing the music and seeing the reaction — would have been nice," said Hellebuyck. "It's out of my hands." It has not been welcome homecoming for returning players this season, especially ones who demanded trades.
